verdicts.reasons: Rejected from the density seat. The blocking problem is the open state, which is taller than today on every panel: 130 px vs d04's 106.1 at 373 and 320 (+23.9, +23%), and 240.6 vs 216.7 at 189 and 160. Open is the default on first open, and it is the state anyone doing theme work keeps, so for the common case the fold makes the panel longer, not shorter. The extra row carries no information while open: the summary reads only 'Theme' (AX name 'Theme'), and at 200% zoom a second, near-empty row holds only Change (A-kd-189-open.png). Folded at 160 px, A is 73.3 px because the chip and the scope each drop to their own line (B: 49.8). What A does well: the folded row matches the other section titles, and Change sits outside the fold row. Only a click 3 px above Change folds the band (1 of 5 near misses). Fold memory, Fold all and the pending hide all work. A is the fallback if B's PT01 cannot land, not the preferred shape.

required_changes.change: B: while open, the fold row ends where Change's zone begins. In proto-B.css, replace the open-state padding-right with a margin: `details.hw-look-fold[open] > summary.hw-look-name { margin-right: 72px; padding-right: 0; }`. Leave the folded rule alone: the row stays full width, and Change is hidden inside the fold. Applies at every width, including the under-300 px layout. No markup or copy change.
required_changes.why: RD/MF. In the prototype, the summary box surrounds Change on all sides, so a click just off the 44 x 25 px link folds the band. The link then vanishes with the band, so the person must reopen and aim again. This reproduced on 5 of 5 near misses at 373, 189 and 160 px (d04: 0 of 5). For someone who clicks Change quickly on key after key, this is the likeliest misfire in the panel. In my B3 copy the fix costs 0 px (113/33 at 373, same text width as the prototype) and leaves a dead zone of about 15.5 px left of Change, plus the full row height above and below it.

answers.q1_variant: B with PT01 (blocking) and PT04 (blocking tests), plus PT02 and PT03. Folded, B's row reads '> Theme [chip in the palette it resolves to; Default keeps its link mark and dashed frame] (shared: Void)'. That answers what is drawn (the palette and its name) and where it comes from (the scope in the Text-select idiom), in one 33 px row: 73 px less than today at 373 and 167 px less at 160. Open, it is today's line with a marker: 'Theme Default (shared: Void) ... Change', for +6.9 px. A answers the same questions but pays 23.9 px on every open panel for a row that only says 'Theme'. C pays 8 px more folded at 373 and 26 px more at 160 for the same information. On the most frequent theme task (pick a theme for this key), B costs one extra Tab stop and one more key press than today (10 vs 9 to pick Ember from the page top; d04's 9 is INFERRED from its Tab path). Pointer: 1 click open, 2 clicks folded. The second click is paid once per run of keys, because opening the band is remembered for the next key panel (MEASURED). The chips move 6.9 px down with B vs 23.9 with A, which matters for muscle memory from d04.
answers.q2_fold_all: Yes: Open all, Fold all and Alt-click should include the band. All three prototypes already do, and it works (MEASURED in A, B, C and B3). Fold all folds the band, and the folded row still shows the chip and scope, so the resolved theme stays on screen as the owner's rule requires. Fold all's aria-disabled becomes true only once the band is folded too. Open all reopens it. Alt-click on the band row, or on Reading, folds or opens everything including the band. With everything folded, the key panel fits the 410 px viewport, and Reading's title sits at 122 px (B) vs 195 in d04, where the band could not fold. For someone who folds everything, the band is the largest single block (106 to 113 px, over a quarter of the 410 px panel), so leaving it out would make 'Fold all' untrue exactly where it matters most. The memory is per panel kind: folding the band on a key panel folds it on the next key panel (Reading stayed open) but not on a dial panel. That suits working across many keys: one click per kind per plugin session, re-done after an app or plugin restart as with every other section.
answers.q3_hidden_until_answer: Acceptable. MEASURED on the sim: the band's chips first appear at 40 ms in d04 and at 30/40/29/42 ms in A/B/C/B3 with no plugin delay. With a 250 ms plugin delay they appear at 289 ms in d04 and at 289/313/288/289 ms in A/B/C/B3. The reason: in d04 the theme line and the chips already wait for the plugin's themes answer (renderThemeLine and renderGallery return until themesConfig arrives), so hiding the band until the fold answer adds no wait anyone could see. It also prevents the real hazard: an open band snapping shut under the pointer when a remembered fold arrives. INFERRED for the real app: the fold answer and the themes answer are both local round trips to the same plugin, and the 300 ms cap still bounds the hide. In the sim one delay covered all replies, so the real app's ordering is unproven.
answers.q4_accessibility: What the row must say, MEASURED in Chrome's AX tree: the native summary (role from details/summary, so no ARIA is needed) with expanded state and the name 'Theme' + resolved name + scope. In B: 'Theme Default (shared: Void)', expanded true open and false folded; 'Theme Ultraviolet (set on this key)'; 'Theme Default (shared: Paper)'; 'Theme "aurora-borealis-x" (unknown; draws Void)'. A says only 'Theme' while open and the same full string folded. The cloned mini chip must not add a second 'Default'. In B it doesn't, because the open-state name span is display:none while folded, but textContent still doubles it, so tests must read the AX name (PT04). The radiogroup keeps name 'Theme' and its description ('Follows the shared theme, now Void.'). Change keeps aria-label 'Change the shared theme'. The extra Tab stop is justified: a disclosure must be operable from the keyboard (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, SB; WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure pattern: the toggle is a button in the Tab order). Its cost is one stop while open (the checked chip is the 4th stop vs 3rd in d04). Folded, it saves a stop (Reading is the 3rd stop vs 4th in d04). Enter and Space both toggle, focus stays on the row, and nothing is written (MEASURED). Change passes WCAG 2.5.8 on its own size (44 x 25 px), but only PT01 stops near misses from folding the band.
answers.q5_edge_states: No reading (key): folded, the row says 'Theme [Default] (shared: Void)' while the key draws its 'Pick a sensor' prompt on fixed black. The help 'Shows on the key once a reading is picked.' is inside the fold, so it is hidden. The header face and 'No reading selected' state the truth right above, so I accept it. Open adds the same 19 px help as d04 (B 132.1 vs d04 125.2 at 373). Unknown stored theme: no chip is checked, so the folded row shows the stored id and '(unknown; draws Void)' as text only. The resolved theme is named, not drawn, which is acceptable for a downgrade-only state. A is 31.2 px folded at 373, B is 33. At 160, B is 77.5 folded and 334.5 open vs d04's 284.1, because of the 72 px reserve beside Change. At 320, d04, B and C alike ellipsize the name while open (not new). Paper shared: the mini chip draws in Paper's light palette with a dark name and a visible dashed frame on the dark panel, and the row reads '(shared: Paper)'. Nothing is clipped at any width. 200% zoom, open/folded px: at 189, B 216.7/49.8 (d04 216.7), A 240.6/53.1, C 216.7/57.8, B3 218.8/51.8. At 160, B 233.5/49.8 (d04 216.7), A 240.6/73.3, C 233.5/75.9, B3 233.5/51.8. No horizontal overflow and no clipped element in any state, width or variant. I tried moving Change to its own line at zoom (B2): it cost 22.9 px open at 189 and only helped the unknown-theme case, so I dropped it.
